Copy of it has been served  on the learned Counsel for the Writ Petitioner and  the same is taken on record.

3. Answering the queries of this Court,
 the Revenue Divisional Officer has stated in the  Written Instructions that the Award has not been  passed.
4. Admittedly, an extent of Ac.0.22   cents (in two different parcels) has been acquired  by the Official Respondents vide Notification  dated:10.12.2018.

At Serial Nos. 22 and  24 (Ex.P.2), the property of the Writ Petitioner is  clearly reflected.

Despite the fact that the  possession has been taken by the Official  Respondents long ago (in the year 2020), the  latest Written Instructions would indicate that an  Award has not yet been passed by the Official  Respondents.

sentences.text: It is also stated that at  present no land acquisition funds have been  allocated by the Government.
5. It is a fact that the Writ Petitioner has  lost possession of his land in the year 2020.
The  proceedings were allowed to lapse after utilizing  the land of the Writ Petitioner for the concerned  project, which is now irreversible.
The  Proceedings were allowed to lapse on account of  shortage of funds as it is stated in the Written  Instruction.
The Writ Petitioner, is therefore, left  high and dry
because the Writ Petitioner would
neither be able to use the land nor would get any  compensation in the near future.
Prima facie, it  3 SL.
DATE ORDER OFFICE NO.
NOTE  appears to this Court that the Award was not
deliberately
passed because the State  Government has not made any arrangement or  provision for allocating any budget for paying  compensation to the rightful claimants.

It is the  opinion of this Court that the rightful compensation  ought to have been disbursed to all the affected  persons at the earliest to enable such persons,
 including the Writ Petitioner, to utilize the said  amount for appropriate purposes.

6. The present scenario would reflect a  very sorry state of affairs inasmuch as they  indicate that the Government intends to now issue  fresh Acquisition Notification and the Writ  Petitioner is expected to wait for the Final Award  to be passed.

It is therefore 'a writing on the wall'
 that the Writ Petitioner will have to wait for an  indefinite period of time to receive his rightful due.

On the face of it, this Court is of the opinion that  the Respondent Government has acted with  'malice in law' (implied malice) with respect to the  Writ Petitioner in acquiring the land and changing  the geographical appearance of it thus making it  unworthy for any utilization without paying the  deserving compensation.

sentences.text: The Hon'ble  Apex Court, in Para 10 of the said Judgment, had  explained the scope and role of Rule of Law to  protect a common man against the might of the  State.
An ordinary citizen or a common man is hardly equipped to match the might of the State or its instrumentalities.
That is provided by the rule of law.
It acts as a check on arbitrary and capricious exercise of power.

In Rookes v. Barnard [1964 AC 1129 : (1964) 1 All ER 367, 410] it was observed by Lord Devlin, the servants of the government are also the servants of the people and the use of their power must always be subordinate to their duty of service.

entities.text: Rookes v. Barnard [1964 AC 1129 : (1964) 1 All ER 367, 410]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A public functionary if he acts maliciously or oppressively and the exercise of power results in harassment and agony then it is not an exercise of power but its abuse.
No law provides protection against it.
He who is responsible for it must suffer it.
Compensation or damage as explained earlier may arise even when the officer discharges his duty honestly and bona fide.
But when it arises due to arbitrary or capricious behaviour then it loses its individual character and assumes social SL.
DATE ORDER OFFICE NO.
NOTE significance.
Harassment of a common man by public authorities is socially abhorring and legally impermissible.
It may harm him personally but the injury to society is far more grievous.

In the same paragraph, the Hon'ble Apex Court, while referring to the treaties of Professor H.W.R. Wade, in his book 'Administrative Law', had explained scope of 'misfeasance by public authorities'.
9.

Legal malice 25.

sentences.text: It is an act done wrongfully and wilfully without reasonable or probable cause, and not necessarily an act done from ill feeling and spite.
It is a deliberate act in disregard to the rights of others.
Where malice is attributed to the State, it can never be a case of personal ill will or spite on the part of the State.
It is an act which is taken with an oblique or indirect object.
It means exercise of statutory power for "purposes foreign to those for which it is in law intended".

sentences.text: In this view of the matter, this Court would contemplate to initiate departmental action against the Officers responsible for the present situation, if it so emerges in the enquiry that there is gross negligence leading to the sufferance of the Writ Petitioner.

The Principal Secretary, Revenue Department and the Commissioner, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (Land Acquisition) is directed to answer as to why an investigation should not be initiated for identifying the Officers responsible and for initiating departmental action for gross negligence leading to gross dereliction of duty for bringing about the present situation where the Writ Petitioner is now left high and dry at the SL.
DATE ORDER OFFICE
NO. NOTE cross-road without being able to see the light at the end of the tunnel for indefinite period of time.
11. Learned Asst. Government Pleader is directed to convey a copy of this Order to the Respondent Nos.1 and 2 forthwith for immediate response.
Respondent Nos.1 and 2 shall file Affidavits well before the next date of listing 12.
